item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q003_actin_like_atpase_divergence","answer":"SCOPe places the catalytic domains of actin/HSP70, hexokinase, and glycerol kinase in separate families—c.55.1.1, c.55.1.2, and c.55.1.3, respectively—within the same Actin-like ATPase superfamily (c.55.1) and fold (c.55), in the alpha-and-beta class. Superfamily membership supports remote homology and a probable common evolutionary origin, including a conserved ATP-binding/catalytic structural core despite substantial sequence and functional divergence. It does not justify transferring substrate specificity, cellular role, detailed catalytic residues, oligomeric state, or family-level annotation among actin/HSP70, hexokinase, and glycerol kinase. Cross-family structures may provide cautious fold-level templates, but family-specific insertions, conformational changes, and active-site features require independent sequence, structural, and biochemical evidence.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
